summary: You can uninstall the Copilot app and remove it from the taskbar, but users widely report it silently reinstalling itself. The durable fix is a registry policy, not a settings toggle.

steps.path: Settings → Apps → Installed apps → Copilot → Uninstall (if listed). Also right-click the taskbar → Taskbar settings → hide Copilot.
Block the silent reinstall and the Copilot surface via policy keys (requires admin; back up first):
steps.code:
reg add "HKCU\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsCopilot" /v TurnOffWindowsCopilot /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ContentDeliveryManager" /v SilentInstalledAppsEnabled /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f

steps.path: Enterprise: use the equivalent GPO / Intune policy instead of per-user registry edits.

collateral: registry edits are unsupported for consumers and can be reverted by feature updates
Copilot has been reported to come back after cumulative updates — re-check monthly
whyTheyDidIt: Copilot usage in Windows is the headline number Microsoft reports; a default off switch would flatten it.

sources.label: Consumer Reports — disabling Copilot in Windows 11
